solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unselfish, good to score inside box

indicators.note: inside tells us the first piece sits within the box, which is split open around it

parts.note: a crate is a box for goods
in football a player must be onside for a goal to count, so onside is what is good to score

explanation.surface: Praise for a footballer who scores from inside the box yet still plays for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal. 'box' suggests the penalty area beside 'score', but it is a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: A considerate person thinks of others first, which is the same as being unselfish.

indicators.note: after places the banking word behind the gold word in the answer

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
an aircraft banks when it leans over in a turn

explanation.surface: A continental city whose banks chase gold.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; 'banks' is a verb here, tilting as a plane does, not money houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a city on the Loire in France, so it is a European city.

indicators.note: bust means broken, so the letters of the two words are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A small chest that is broken turns out to be a counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' reads as breasts beside 'chest', but it signals breaking up TINYCHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something synthetic is artificial rather than natural, so fake in the sense of man-made.

indicators.note: revealing tells us the answer is shown lying within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Something ends up getting away, exposing a con.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across enD UP ESCaping.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to deceive them, so dupes is a verb meaning tricks.

clue.text: More weather-beaten sailor up on deck

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the sailor word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
a deck of a ship or a bus is one tier

explanation.surface: A sailor high on the ship's deck gets more battered by the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the reversal signal, apt in a down answer; 'on' means placed above, since the reversed sailor sits over the deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty can mean shabby and worn, so rattier is comparative: more tatty or battered.

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for heavyweight is to be said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a titan is a giant, a person of great size or importance

explanation.surface: A boxing heavyweight is said to have seized up with cramp.
explanation.walkthrough: TITAN, said aloud, gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to confine or restrict, as to tighten is to draw closer and constrict.

definitions.meaning: to return a favour or feeling is to give back in kind
to match someone's gesture is to respond in the same way

explanation.definitionFit: To reciprocate is to give back the same, so both returning and matching describe it.

indicators.note: about means going round, so the facial feature surrounds the work word

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A piece about a work by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'from' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin was a Polish composer of piano music.

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so the eternity word wraps the other pieces

parts.note: an eon is an immeasurably long period, an eternity
Che Guevara is the stock crossword revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary left wing holds its ground for all time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' is the container signal; the revolutionary and left pieces go in together.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or rank in an organisation, so a position in a hierarchy.

clue.text: Send back for example, a first soup

indicators.note: send back tells us the whole string of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: top means first, as in top of the class

explanation.surface: A diner returns a first course of soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send back' turns EG+A+TOP into the answer; it reads like returning a dish to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Potage is the French term for a thick soup.

clue.text: Given a test, I organised research

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters of the fodder words are arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone sat an exam and then set about some study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges GIVENATESTI.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate is to examine or inquire into, which is to research a matter.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP stands for Member of Parliament
each means one by one, individually

explanation.surface: Charging a member of parliament on their own.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach an official is to formally charge them with misconduct, so to accuse.

clue.text: Struck and slapped initally with glove

indicators.note: initally (initially, as printed) tells us to take only the opening letter of slapped

parts.note: a mitten is a kind of glove

explanation.surface: Someone was hit, slapped with a glove as a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struck' looks like hit, but it means lovestruck; 'initally' is printed thus, meaning initially.
explanation.definitionFit: Smitten is the old past participle of smite, so struck, and also means struck by love.

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
ends are the boundaries or limits of something

explanation.surface: A batter's big hits pile up runs and boundaries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a boundary is a hit to the edge of the field; here it just means ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart violently, so rends means smashes or rips.

definitions.meaning: play is the slack or allowed movement in a mechanism
patience is putting up with others without complaint

explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance means both a permitted margin of movement in engineering and a forbearing attitude.

clue.text: One may get a damsel in trouble!

definitions.text: One may get a damsel in trouble!

indicators.note: trouble means disorder, so the letters of the words before it are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rake whose charm leads young women astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' shuffles ADAMSELIN; the whole clue also describes a womaniser, who may get a damsel into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' man is a womaniser, the kind of seducer who might leave a girl in trouble.

clue.text: Swayed a month back after do with Bordeaux?

indicators.note: after places the month piece behind the do and Bordeaux pieces

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them
Bordeaux is a French wine, and vin is French for wine

indicators.note: back tells us the month abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: Dec is short for December, a month

explanation.surface: A party with claret, and a month later someone has been won over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEC into CED. 'do' looks like a party but means swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being convinced is being persuaded, so swayed in the sense of won over by argument.

indicators.note: first places the number abbreviation ahead of the play word

parts.note: to strum is to play a guitar casually

explanation.surface: A band plays a number by The Cure first.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks hint at a doubtful remedy, as a nostrum is.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, so a cure of dubious worth, as the quotation marks suggest.

clue.text: From Italy, china includes Italian fake

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: includes means the friend word holds the other piece within it

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, a friend
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: Porcelain from Italy contains a counterfeit Italian piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' reads as porcelain but is rhyming slang: china plate = mate, a pal, from London's Cockney slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy, so to fake something by copying another's manner.

indicators.note: outside means the premier word sits round the other letter

parts.note: premier means foremost, the best

explanation.surface: Attack the leading Englishman from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts E inside BEST, between S and T. 'premier' looks like a prime minister but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To beset is to attack from all sides, which means the same as assail.

clue.text: Delivered and born before estimated time

indicators.note: before places the born letter ahead of the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: a rough figure is an estimated one

explanation.surface: A baby was delivered and born ahead of its due date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' feels like childbirth, matching 'born', but it means carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Brought is the past tense of bring, so delivered in the sense of carried to someone.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the tears word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: rips are tears in fabric

indicators.note: almost means the everything word loses its last letter

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A gale tears everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RIPS into SPIR; 'almost' cuts ALL to AL. 'Wind' is a verb (rhyming with mind), not a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: To spiral is to coil or twist round, which is what winding means.

clue.text: Police chief following endless stay for trial

indicators.note: following places the Police chief after the trimmed stay word
endless means the word stay loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Sting was the lead singer, the chief, of the band The Police

explanation.surface: A senior officer comes after a long stay for a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police chief' looks like a senior officer, but it is Sting, frontman of the rock band The Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A tasting is a trial sample of food or wine, a small try to judge its quality.

clue.text: Grand redhead with bottom on lawn

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
the head, or first letter, of red is R
ass is slang for bottom

explanation.surface: A grand red-haired person sits with their bottom on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redhead' reads as a ginger person but means the head of the word red.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is what a lawn is made of, so the word stands for the lawn itself.

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is drawn out of the run of clue words that follows

explanation.surface: King Herod brought ruin on the region of Galilee.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across hEROD IN Galilee.
explanation.definitionFit: Eroding means wearing away, and as a noun that is gradual degradation.

parts.note: Sir Francis Drake is said to have finished his game of bowls before sailing to fight the Spanish fleet; his foe at sea, the main, was that fleet

explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish Armada was the fleet Drake faced in 1588, his opponent on the main or sea.

clue.text: Asylum seeker perhaps shouting, put on plane

indicators.note: put on places the shouting word after the plane word in this across answer

parts.note: a MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a rant is angry shouting

explanation.surface: Someone seeking asylum is put on a plane, shouting in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A migrant moves from one country to another, of whom an asylum seeker is one example.

indicators.note: crazy means wild, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some primate has gone mad, an ape after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges PRIMATESONE. 'ape' looks like an animal alongside 'Primate', but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to mimic them, which is to impersonate.
